He should bathe the imperishable Viṣṇu with pure, slightly warm water, / and smear the limbs of Viṣṇu with very fine sandal-paste.
He should worship the Lord of the universe, the God of gods, who bears the discus; / he should clean the vessels and leave them free of water.
Having bathed the Lord of the world with slightly warm water, / his body should be carefully wiped with a divine cloth.
If one bathes Keśava with slightly warm waters / in the month of Māgha, O best of the twice-born, I shall state his reward:
Freed from all sins accumulated across many births, / he enjoys all happiness in this world, and in the end goes to the abode of Hari.
Having carefully washed the vessels and made them pure with water, / heed the merit of him who worships the Lord of the world:
Having enjoyed all desires in this world, free from all diseases, / in the end he remains in the abode of Keśava for thousands of yugas.
At dawn and at dusk, before the discus-bearing Lord, / a Vaiṣṇava person should place a blazing, smokeless fire.
To ward off the cold in Māgha, a Vaiṣṇava should kindle a fire / before Viṣṇu in the evening and in the morning. Hear the reward of that:
Having enjoyed all desires here, accompanied by sons and grandsons, / in the end he goes to the city of Viṣṇu, difficult even for the gods to attain.
Viṣṇu is just like one's own self; there is no doubt in this. / When Keśava, the God of gods, is sleeping upon his couch,
just as a mortal wards off cold for himself, / what would the supreme god Viṣṇu, well-pleased, not grant to him / who bathes Janārdana with milk in the month of Māgha?
so should he dispel the cold for the discus-bearer with a divine cloth.
He who bathes the four-armed [Lord] with coconut-water and milk / and worships him even once in Māgha, I will proclaim his reward:
Having delivered ten million ancestors sinking in the ocean of hell, / which is difficult to cross because of one’s own deeds, he goes to the realm of the discus-bearer.
In the month of Māgha, on the bright fifth day, O best of the twice-born, / and on the eleventh and the fifteenth, worship of Hari is especially [meritorious].
Day after day in the month of Māgha, milk-rice along with incense / should be offered to the God of gods, who holds the lotus, the enemy of Mura.
To him who offers milk-rice accompanied by incense to the discus-bearer in Māgha, / I declare the meritorious fruit; hear, O Vaiṣṇava Jaimini!
In the end, having gone to the city of Viṣṇu for four manvantaras, / he enjoys delightful pleasures by the grace of the discus-bearing Lord.
Having returned to the earth, he becomes a universal emperor; / having enjoyed pleasure for a very long time, upon death he goes to the abode of Hari.
Or on the fifth, on the seventh, and on the eleventh, O Jaimini, / an incapable Vaiṣṇava may offer rice-pudding to the enemy of Mura.
More especially during the bright fortnight than the dark fortnight, O best of the twice-born, / one should offer food to the enemy of Mura on these lunar days in the bright fortnight.
He who, even for a single day in Māgha, offers milk-rice with cakes / to Viṣṇu, the conqueror of the Daityas—Hari is not difficult for him to attain.
Whatever is offered in the month of Māgha for the pleasure of the twice-born / becomes imperishable for a man; there is no doubt about this.
Action performed in the month of Māgha, whether good or indeed evil, / has no destruction, O brāhmaṇa, even in hundreds of manvantaras.
He who worships the Lord of Kamalā in Māgha with a campaka flower, / freed from all sins, goes to the supreme abode.
For as many golden flowers as are given to the discus-bearing Lord, / for that many thousands of yugas does one dwell in the abode of Viṣṇu.
The reward that comes from giving gold equal [in weight] to Mount Meru, / that reward is attained by worshiping Hari with a single golden flower.
A golden flower, O best of brāhmaṇas, is always dear to Keśava; / especially in the month of Māgha, it is pure and dear to Keśava.
He by whom Hari is not worshiped with divine golden flowers / shall be bereft of jewels, gold, and the like, birth after birth.
I will tell in detail the fruit of the campaka flower; / hear, O best of the twice-born, this supreme legendary history.
There was a king named Suvarṇa, powerful and knowledgeable in all scriptures, / [renowned] throughout all Āryāvarta for the splendor of a brāhmaṇa.
Through royal splendor, learning, and youth, that ruler of the earth / became exceedingly intoxicated, O sage among brāhmaṇas, and was constantly devoted to sin.
Following the words of heretical ministers, even when they were blameless, O twice-born, / virtuous people were punished by that king out of greed for wealth.
Surrounded by singing, instrumental music, and the like, / he squandered all the wealth acquired unlawfully, devoid of sacrifices and charity.
He did not support his kinsmen, nor did he feed the gods and the twice-born, / nor did he satisfy supplicants, being always bewildered by sin.
Always intent on evil deeds, he never performed worship of guests; / and that king, an abode of sins, constantly went away from his temple.
The sins committed by that man—those of thoughtless persons— / would anyone be able to enumerate them even in a hundred years?
Once that protector of the earth, completely infatuated with desire, / went to a courtesan’s dwelling at midnight, his mind set on evil.
Then, seeing the ruler of the earth arriving, the woman named Ujjvalā / rose up quickly on the bed and bowed to his feet.
Having washed his pair of feet with water from a pitcher, / she embraced that king with her arms and seated him upon the couch.
Drenched by streams of the nectar of her love, that lord of the earth / sat upon that bed with her, filled with eagerness.
Then that courtesan, smiling in her prime of youth, / lovingly gave him campaka flowers herself to the ruler of the earth.
From the flower garland, a single flower fell from the king's hand / onto the surface of the earth, its fragrance pervading all directions.
Seeing that fallen flower, the king, out of great agitation, / said, 'Oṃ, homage to Nārāyaṇa,' preceded by the syllable Oṃ.
Through the utterance of the word 'To Nārāyaṇa' / and through offering the golden flower, all the sins of that king were destroyed.
Then all the villagers, coming together at an invincible hour, / killed him in that very night while he was inside the courtesan's house.
Then, to carry off that king, the foremost of all sinners, / the son of Vivasvat, exceedingly enraged, sent his servants.
Commanded by him, the messengers, holding nooses and clubs in their hands, / arrived with great speed, their eyes red with anger.
The messengers of Yama made an effort to lead him to their own realm; / then the servants of Nārāyaṇa, bearing conch, discus, and mace,
Mounted on Garuḍa, they arrived to lead that ruler of the earth away. / Seeing that king restrained in fetters, Viṣṇu's attendants,
Mighty in strength, struck Yama's messengers with discs and maces. / Placing him on a celestial chariot, they blew their peerless conches.
Mounted likewise on the chariot, adorned with a garland of tulasī, / Wearing yellow silk garments and embellished with golden ornaments,
Praised by hosts of sages who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / Surrounded by Viṣṇu's messengers, he went to Hari's world.
Then Viṣṇu himself arose, and with his four long arms / Embraced that king, O best of the twice-born, and spoke:
The Blessed Lord said: / Speak of your welfare, O king, best among all virtuous souls! / What wish of yours is to be fulfilled? Command it now!
He who says even once, “Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa,” / Must always be protected by me; he is my brother, he is my father.
Whatever mortal at any time remembers my name, “Nārāyaṇa,” / I fulfill all his desires, as a son does for his father.
You are my devotee, O best of kings; therefore, disclose your marvelous / Desire, my friend! What may I give you now?
The king said: / Everything has indeed been granted by you, O ocean of mercy, without a doubt! / Even sinner that I was, I have attained your abode, so difficult to reach.
Pleased with these words of his, the lord of Kamalā / Affectionately seated the ruler of the earth; listen to that:
Then, with golden ornaments fashioned by Viśvakarman, / The compassionate one personally arranged an adornment for him.
Then, with various divine eatables exceedingly hard to obtain, / That king was gratified by Viṣṇu, who is exceedingly forbearing.
In this way, that king remained daily in Viṣṇu's abode / For a thousand manvantaras and nine hundred years.
That king, intent on dharma, protected his subjects; / He constantly worshipped Hari with supreme devotion,
With lovely campaka flowers and various offerings of food. / At the end of his lifespan, that ruler of the earth met his death in the water of the Jāhnavī,
And attained liberation through the grace of the one who bears the disc in his hand. / Vyāsa said: / O brahmin, the power of the campaka flower has thus been proclaimed.
By worshipping Hari with campakas, even sinful people become liberated. / When the Blessed Lord Hari is worshipped with a blossoming campaka flower,
He soon grants the supreme abode, O brahmin-sage! / Those who worship the Supreme Self, whether intentionally or unintentionally,
They too, freed from all sins, go to the supreme abode.
When Hari is pleased, no one remains a sinner, since even that king who had committed sins / Attained liberation through Murāri's mercy, crossing over this deep cosmic ocean.
A mortal who worships Nārāyaṇa, whose eyes are wide as lotus petals, / With divine, fragrant golden blossoms with devotion and supreme reverence, leaves behind sin and attains that [abode].

title: ekādaśo'dhyāyaḥ
text_mt: Vyāsa said: / According to what rite Hari must always be worshipped, O Jaimini, / That I shall tell you, O brahmin-sage; listen attentively, dear child.
Rising from bed at dawn, taking a vessel of water, / The wise man should go outside, having covered his head with a cloth.
There, facing the northern direction, silent, having placed his sacred thread / Over his ears, seated, the wise man should discharge feces and urine.
In a temple of a deity, on a path, in cowpens, and in courtyards, / On a public street, in ploughed land, at the root of darbha grass, and in a front yard,
On the bank of a river, at the foot of a sacred fig tree, and likewise in a forest, / And in the beds of tanks and wells, one should not discharge feces or urine.
The sun, the moon, brahmins, cows, and the ten directions— / While discharging feces and urine, the wise man does not look at these.
Earth dug up by mice and the like, situated inside a hole, / And ploughed by a plowshare—one must never take this for the purpose of purification.
Fetching water from a water-source, the discerning man should perform purification; / A wise man does not perform purification having placed his foot in the water.
Facing south at night, the wise man should attend to the bodily necessity; / Having covered his head with a cloth, he should then perform purification.
One application of clay is to be given to the penis, and three to the anus; / Seven to the left hand, and ten to both hands by the wise.
Six applications of clay are to be given to the feet by the discerning. / Having performed the purification rites, the wise man should clean his teeth
And scrape his tongue with tooth-cloths and the like. / Having turned facing south, or likewise facing west,
One should not clean one's teeth; if one does, one will go to hell. / With the middle finger, the ring finger, and the thumb, O twice-born,
One should clean one's teeth; never with the forefinger. / From the aśvattha, the banyan tree, the dhātrī, or the kaithika, the wise man
Should not make a tooth-cleaning twig, nor likewise from the trees sacred to Indra and the gods; / The daily fruit of his rites is entirely destroyed.
He who cleans his teeth at the time of bathing, O Jaimini— / His ancestors, the gods, and the divine sages depart hopeless.
He who cleans his teeth at midday or in the afternoon— / The deities do not accept his worship, nor the ancestors his water.
He who cleans his teeth in a lotus-pond at the time of bathing / Is to be known as an outcaste until he sees the Gaṅgā.
He who cleans his teeth after the venerable sun has arisen— / Consuming that tooth-stick, his ancestors depart full of sorrow.
On a fast day, O brahmin, and on the day of an ancestral rite, / A man who cleans his teeth [with a stick] does not attain that fruit.
In the morning, the wise man should clean his teeth and tongue with a cloth; / He should rinse twelve times with water, O chief of brahmins.
On a fast day and an ancestral rite, performing the cleaning of teeth / In accordance with this rule, O Jaimini, a mortal obtains the full fruit.
Having performed the evacuation in accordance with this rule, the farsighted man / Should then go to his house and cast off his night-garment.
Then, seated at the door of the shrine, pure, the wise man / Should remember God Nārāyaṇa, the infinite, the supreme lord:
“O Rāma! O dark-bodied Viṣṇu! O Nārāyaṇa full of compassion! / O Janārdana! O abode of the universe! Remove my sin, O Keśava!
O wearer of yellow garments! O Ananta! O Padmanābha! O embodiment of the world! / O Vāmana! O Lord of the bowed! O all-pervading one, be my refuge!
O Dāmodara! O best of the Yadus! O Śrī Kṛṣṇa! O ocean of mercy! / O lotus-eyed one! O lord of gods! O Vāsudeva, show compassion!
O one whose emblem is Garuḍa! O Govinda! O supporter of the universe! O bearer of the mace! / O conch-handed one! O disc-handed one! O lotus-handed one! Remove my distress!
O delight of Lakṣmī! O Vaikuṇṭha! O Hṛṣīkeśa! O best of the gods! / O Puruṣottama! O enemy of Kaṃsa! O enemy of Kaiṭabha! Dispel my fear!
O lord of Śrī! O Śrīdhara! O all-pervading one! O bestower of prosperity! O causer of prosperity! O Mādhava! / O supreme Brahman! O supreme abode! Be my refuge, O imperishable one!”
Having thus performed the remembrance of glorious Viṣṇu, O best of the twice-born, the wise man, / Entering into his dwelling with folded hands, speaks thus:
“O Lord! O lord of Śrī! O Kṛṣṇa! O joy of Devakī! O master! / Relinquish sleep, O Jagannātha! The time of morning has come!”
Then, having cast off sleep, the wise man should contemplate in his mind / the son of Devakī accompanied by Lakṣmī as if risen upon His couch.
Then the Vaiṣṇava should offer to Kṛṣṇa a covered, divine vessel / filled with water for rinsing His mouth.
Just as servants serve their master for livelihood, / even so the wise serve the Supreme Lord.
Indeed, he who serves the Lord of the universe in the form of a servant, / O brahmin sage, his desire is accomplished without delay.
Just as attendants perform service to their master with reverence, / so the wise always serve Lord Hari.
If a man worships Viṣṇu according to his own whims, devoid of reverence, / he is a bad servant, and it will not bear fruit, O brahmin.
Therefore, O best of brahmins, service to the Lord of Kamalā / must always be performed with promptness by a man desiring absolute liberation.
The Vaiṣṇava person should remove from Hari's body in the morning / the withered flower offerings, the night garments, and the stale fragrance.
Then he himself should sweep that temple of the deity; / the wise man should gradually cleanse it with a broom.
As many particles of dust as go out from that abode, / for so many hundreds of manvantaras a person will dwell in Viṣṇu's house.
Even a slayer of a brahmin who sweeps Hari's house / goes to the supreme abode; what need of many words?
Likewise, O brahmin, the wise man should smear that house of Viṣṇu / with moist cow dung, remembering Lord Nārāyaṇa.
He who smears the temple of Keśava, / of his merit I shall speak in brief; listen, O Jaimini.
As many specks of dust as are destroyed there, O best of brahmins, / for so many thousands of kalpas he will dwell happy in Viṣṇu's house.
A person having swept and smeared Viṣṇu's house / attains the supreme abode; what need to speak of the fruit of worshipping the Lord?
When, due to an obstacle from the king or deity, he is unable to do so himself, / he should employ his lawful wife in Viṣṇu's house.
Or he should appoint in the temple of the deity / his own devoted, virtuous son, or his brother, or his sister.
He himself should wash the articles for Hari's worship with great care / seven times with pure water, or three times.
Copper vessels are purified with acid, bell-metal vessels with ashes, / and iron vessels with fire; of this there is no doubt.
A wealthy person who bathes Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the universe, / with water kept in an iron vessel—with him Keśava is not pleased.
Or if it happens out of ignorance, he is purified by bathing in the Gaṅgā; / in prosperity, O best of brahmins, the rule must always be observed.
In misfortune there is no strict rule: such is the determination in the scriptures. / When a conch, carefully washed, touches the ground again,
then, O chief of brahmins, that conch is not purified even by being washed a hundred times. / Having thus carefully washed the worship materials of the wielder of the discus,
and taking the materials for bathing, he should go to a pond to bathe. / He who returns home without having performed the rites of bathing,
on that day the multitude of his ancestors does not obtain water offerings. / If one creates an obstacle for a person going to bathe or eat,
he who does so out of delusion, O best of brahmins, surely goes to hell. / He who, having gone to a pond to bathe, passes feces and urine,
his ancestors will consume feces and urine, of this there is no doubt. / Then, having performed bathing and water offerings according to the rule,
the wise man should return to his own house, remembering Nārāyaṇa. / And then in the courtyard, O brahmin, having washed both feet,
the pure one, best of brahmins, should enter the sanctuary of the deity. / The person who enters the abode with unwashed feet,
his merit acquired over a year is destroyed that very moment. / Having bathed and arrived in the courtyard, the discerning man,
having washed both feet, should therefore enter the house of the deity. / Having sat down, the wise man, with the left hand,
should carefully wash both feet, O brahmin, and then both hands; / foot by foot, O chief of brahmins, and also with the right hand.
And the foolish person who washes them [improperly], Lakṣmī surely abandons him. / Then, being seated, the intelligent man should begin the worship of Keśava,
becoming single-minded, which grants the fruits of all desires. / On a pure seat of deer skin, or on a seat of tiger skin,
or on a mere cloth seat, and likewise on a seat made of kuśa grass, / or seated on a flower seat, he should worship the Lord of Kamalā.
A learned brahmin should not perform the worship of Viṣṇu on a wooden seat. / 'You are held by Viṣṇu, O Earth, and all the worlds are held by you;
therefore, O all-bearing one, give me an excellent place to sit.' / Having spoken thus and spread the seat, the worshipper of Nārāyaṇa should sit down.
Facing south, one should not perform the worship of Viṣṇu. / Having placed in a conch water purified with mantras and fragrant,
he should bathe the beloved of Kamalā, the Lord together with Kamalā. / He who bathes the Lord, Janārdana, with a conch,
I shall tell the fruit thereof; listen, O Jaimini, chief of brahmins. / Freed from sins such as slaying a brahmin, a cow, a woman, or an embryo, and drinking liquor,
he goes to Vaikuṇṭha and truly enjoys every happiness. / If a human being, looking upon Hṛṣīkeśa, worships Him, O brahmin,
he quickly attains that very thing by the grace of the Lord of Kamalā. / In the absence of a conch, however, O chief of brahmins, the wise man,
having placed fragrant water and tulasī in a vessel, should bathe Keśava. / Then, having bathed the God and placed Him on an excellent seat,
he should anoint all His limbs with fragrant sandalpaste, / and protect the body of the wielder of the discus with the paste of tulasī wood.

The person who does so—Hari is always pleased with him.
'This garland of tulasī leaves, bestowing the joy of its own fragrance,

is given to you, O Lord of the Universe; be well pleased forever.'
With this mantra, O best of Brahmins, when Mahāviṣṇu is adorned

with a garland of tulasī leaves, what will he not give when pleased?
Then, the recitation of svastivācana should be performed with Vedic mantras.

And the binding of the directions should be performed by the wise with Puranic mantras:
'May Kṛṣṇa protect in the east; may the son of Devakī [protect] in the south-east;

may the enemy of the Daityas protect in the south; may Madhusūdana [protect] in the south-west;
may the glorious one protect in the intermediate directions; and may the Lord, the bearer of Śrī, protect above;

may the Self of the Universe, merciful in the form of a tortoise, protect below.
Whatever obstacle-makers may arise at the time of worship,

may they all go far away, struck down by the weapon of Hari's name.'
Having thus performed the binding of the directions, then, bowed down with joined palms,

he makes a firm resolve with the mantra about to be spoken:
'O God of gods, O Janārdana, bring this worship begun by me

to fulfillment without obstacles; be pleased, O Supreme Lord.'
Then, having made the resolve, the Vaiṣṇava who knows all reality,

having performed the placement of the limbs and the rest, should meditate in his heart on Nārāyaṇa,
resembling a fresh raincloud, with eyes resembling white lotus flowers,

the god wearing yellow garments, with a smiling, charming face,
adorned with garlands of kadamba flowers, endowed with mighty arms,

wearing earrings, his crest bound with peacock feathers,
enchanting the ten directions with the sweet sound of his flute,

surrounded by cowherd women, abiding in beautiful Vṛndāvana.
Having thus meditated on the Lord of gods, Govinda, who grants all desires,

the Vaiṣṇava should then perform the invocation with a devotional disposition.
For Kṛṣṇa, who has been invoked, the bestower of the four aims of life,

the discerning one should present water for the feet, the respectful offering, and sipping water.
With tender tulasī leaves or delightful flowers, the wise one

should worship the Lord of all gods, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī:
'Salutations to the Fish, to the Tortoise, and to the Boar, salutations, salutations!

Salutations be to you, Hari! Salutations, salutations to Vāmana!
Salutations to Rāma, to Rāma, to Rāma, to the strong one, salutations!

Salutations to the Buddha, the pure one, the compassionate one, salutations, salutations!
Salutations be to you, O Kalki! Salutations to you of manifold forms!

To Nārāyaṇa, to Kṛṣṇa, to Govinda, and to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow,
to Dāmodara, to the God, to the God of gods, salutations to you!

To Hṛṣīkeśa, to the tranquil one, to the one whose foot spans the sky, salutations!
Salutations be to the Lord of Padmā! Salutations to you with lotus-eyes!

Salutations to you, Ananta! Salutations to the one whose hand holds the mace!
To you whose banner bears Garuḍa, salutations to you, discus in hand!

Salutations to you, lotus in hand! To Acyuta, salutations, salutations!
Salutations to you, enemy of the Daityas, bestower of all desires!

To Mādhava, to the Lord of gods, to Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self,
to the diadem-wearer, to the earring-wearer, salutations ever be to Hari!

Salutations to you, Blessed Lord; his vehicle is named Garuḍa—
with the mantra: "Salutations to Garuḍa," the discerning one [worships it].

Salutations to the conch, to the discus, and to the mace, salutations, salutations!
Salutations to the lotus, to the sword, to Nandaka, salutations, salutations!'
Having thus worshipped the lord of gods along with his wife, along with his mount, / and along with his weapon, the wise person should then repeat the eight-syllable mantra:

Then, having recited the eight-syllable mantra with his own devotion, the wise one
should then present varied and excellent food-offerings to Govinda,

and incense, a lamp, and betel to Viṣṇu, the God of gods.
The Vaiṣṇava person should present other offerings as well.

The one who gives incense scented with sandalwood and agallochum to Murāri, O best of Brahmins,
his desire is swiftly accomplished.

The one who gives incense scented with clarified butter to Hari, O Brahmin,
freed from millions of sins, would go to Viṣṇu's abode.

The one who gives incense scented with bdellium to Nārāyaṇa,
he goes to the supreme abode, which is difficult even for the gods to attain.

The one who offers a lamp with clarified butter, or with sesame oil,
Keśava removes all of his sin in the twinkling of an eye.

The one who gives betel scented with camphor to the wielder of the discus,
for him, O best of Brahmins, liberation is achieved, O Jaimini.

The one who offers betel combined with catechu,
having enjoyed all pleasures here, goes in the end to the abode of Hari.

Having offered betel furnished with liquorice and sweet fennel, and with nutmeg and other [spices], to Hari,
a mortal attains heaven.

Having placed water in a conch, a Vaiṣṇava person should perform circumambulation of Viṣṇu
with the mantra about to be spoken, O Jaimini:
"O Janārdana, friend of the world, protector of those who have come for refuge, / grant me, O Lord, to be a servant of the servant of a servant of your servant."

The fruit of merit of the one who circumambulates Nārāyaṇa with this mantra,
I shall state in brief; listen, O Jaimini.

Whatever sins there are, such as the slaying of a Brahmin, and whatever great [crimes],
all of them are destroyed at each step of the circumambulation.

As many steps as a man takes with devotion in circumambulating Viṣṇu,
for that many thousands of kalpas he rejoices with Viṣṇu.

As many steps as one walks slowly in circumambulating Hari,
at every step a mortal attains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

Whatever fruit there may be from circumambulating the whole world,
from circumambulating Hari the fruit is ten million times greater than that.

And the one who circumambulates his own body in the presence of Nārāyaṇa,
he too attains that fruit; what need is there of many other words?

The wise man should not cross the soma-channel in circumambulating Śambhu;
when one crosses it, O Brahmin, that worship becomes fruitless.

The one who circles Hari once in the manner of circumambulation,
in birth after birth, O best of Brahmins, he certainly becomes a universal monarch.

The one who performs circumambulation of Viṣṇu twice, O Brahmin,
attains the state of Indra in three days; of this there is no doubt.

The person who performs circumambulation of Viṣṇu twice,
freed from all sins, would enter the body of Mādhava.
One should wave a conch filled with water over Keśava, O Jaimini; / in the end, having gone to the abode of the gods, he will be praised by the deities.

The one who bows down seven times to Keśava like a staff upon the ground,
the sin resting in his body is reduced to ashes that very moment.

The one who bows down to Janārdana, placing joined palms on his head,
to him Viṣṇu, the Lord of Lakṣmī, gives the supreme abode.

Of mortals who bow down to Hari, casting all limbs upon the ground,
listen, O Brahmin-sage, as I declare the power of merit:

as long as the body of mortals is adorned with dust of the earth,
for that many thousands of kalpas they remain in Hari's presence.

Then the flower-remains of Keśava are given to the Vaiṣṇavas.
I shall declare those Vaiṣṇavas; listen, O best of men, Jaimini:
Śuka, Sūta, and also Vyāsa, Nārada, the sage Kapila, / Prahlāda and Ambarīṣa, and also Akrūra and Uddhava—

Vibhīṣaṇa, Hanūmat, and likewise other Vaiṣṇavas as well;
may they receive the flower-remains of Vāsudeva that fulfill all desires.'
Having spoken thus, the Vaiṣṇava should place the remnant of Viṣṇu's offering upon the ground; / then, indeed, he himself takes the remnant of Hari's offering with devotion.
Upon whose head the excellent withered offering of Hari is seen, / he should be known, O best of brahmins, as none other than Hari Himself.
Viṣṇu's food offering is hard to attain, and the withered flower offering destroys sin; / all the gods receive it, so what to say of human beings?
O Jaimini, the Vaiṣṇava who smells a tulasī leaf, / all the sin residing within his body is destroyed.
The fragrance of a tulasī leaf that enters a person's nose / causes misfortunes residing in his body to perish instantly.
He who rejoices having smelled the fragrance of a tulasī leaf, / in his abode there will be everlasting bliss, O best of brahmins.
Having praised the Lord of the universe, the beloved of Kamalā, Acyuta, with hymns, / with joined palms the wise man should then utter this mantra:
'O Nārāyaṇa whose form is the universe, go to Your abode, O Lord of the universe; / go, O God, to Your own place, and be pleased at all times.
This worship of You that has been performed by me according to my ability, / O Lord of gods, O Lord of the universe, let it be flawless by Your grace, O You whose self is the universe!'
Then the wise man should take with devotional disposition the foot-water / of Mahāviṣṇu, the Supreme Self, which destroys all sins.
He who carries even a single drop of the auspicious foot-water of Viṣṇu / has bathed in all holy places; O Jaimini, the truth is spoken.
If one touches the water from Viṣṇu's feet, the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā arises, / since the water of the Gaṅgā, O brāhmaṇa, is the water from Viṣṇu's feet.
There is no untimely death, nor is there fear of disease, / for one who touches the foot-water of great-souled Keśava.
For the destruction of sins and diseases, the water of Viṣṇu's feet is the medicine; / even sinful men should drink it every day.
The Vaiṣṇava person who drinks the water from Viṣṇu's feet, O brāhmaṇa, / the sin residing in his body is destroyed in an instant.
Just as what resides in the body of an embodied being is completely destroyed by medicine, / in the same way is all sin [destroyed] by the water of Viṣṇu's feet.
The pure water from Viṣṇu's feet accompanied by a tulasī leaf— / he who carries it on his head, O brāhmaṇa, I shall tell his merit:
freed from sins such as killing a brāhmaṇa, assuming the form of Viṣṇu, / going at the end to Viṣṇu's realm, he rejoices together with Viṣṇu.
Whatever fruit arises from giving gold equivalent to Mount Meru, / touching the water from Viṣṇu's feet produces a greater fruit than that.
Whatever fruit is attained by people through the gift of ten million horses, / whatever fruit one obtains by giving the earth of seven continents to brāhmaṇas,
that fruit a mortal obtains touching the water from Viṣṇu's feet. / Whatever fruit arises from performing a thousand horse sacrifices,
touching the water from Viṣṇu's feet produces a greater fruit than that. / Whatever merit is celebrated from the gift of a hundred oblong ponds,
touching the foot-water one obtains merit even greater than that. / What is the use of saying much here? It is stated briefly by me:
From the contact with the water of Viṣṇu's feet, a man becomes liberated. / Again and again, O best of brāhmaṇas, it is firmly declared by me:
touching the water from Hari's feet, one does not obtain birth again. / He who [eats] the remainder of food offered to Viṣṇu, which destroys all sins,
who eats it with devotional disposition, goes to the supreme abode. / One who eats the hard-to-attain food offered to Viṣṇu, O best of the twice-born,
sins, even beginning with the murder of a brāhmaṇa, abandon his body. / For him who eats the food offered to Hari, [liberation] becomes subservient like a maidservant.
The realm of liberation, O best of gods, is difficult to attain even by deities; / having worshipped the beloved of Kamalā, not abandoning even a little food-offering,
Viṣṇu leads him without delay to his own form. / What excellence of the food-offering of Mahāviṣṇu shall I tell?
"Eating which even Keśava becomes submissive, O chief of the twice-born; / by this rule, O twice-born, each month [one should worship] Janārdana."
whoever performs the worship of the lord of Kamalā, even if devoid of formal rules, / with devotional disposition, he too becomes dear to Keśava.
Whatever fruit one who knows the rules obtains by worshipping Viṣṇu according to the rules, / according to the prescribed rule, O brāhmaṇa, with abundant food-offerings, O lord,
even when worshipped he is not pleased if devotion is not present. / Whatever devotion someone has toward Janārdana, the god of gods,
just so much is his attainment of fruit; there is no doubt about this. / Whatever worship of Hari is performed without devotion by men on earth,
that worship, O best of brāhmaṇas, lasts only during the time of worship. / Devotion to Hari is rooted in knowledge; the worship of the lord of the world is rooted in devotion.
Worship is the root in the growth of the tree of liberation; adoration of Hari, / which a wise person performs with faith, even if very little,
all that becomes imperishable: every rite accompanied by faith. / He who worships Viṣṇu with devotion even with merely water, O twice-born,
obtains an abode in Viṣṇu's [realm], since Hari is subject to his devotee.
This whole world is worthless; only the worship of Hari is essential, O brāhmaṇa. / Therefore, a person desiring his own auspiciousness should sacrifice with devotion to Kṛṣṇa of boundless form.

title: dvādaśo'dhyāyaḥ
text_mt: Vyāsa said: / In Phālguna, O best of brāhmaṇas, a Vaiṣṇava person should worship / with devotional disposition glorious Kṛṣṇa, who is praised by the gods, every day.
He who bathes the son of Devakī with clarified butter in Phālguna, / I shall proclaim his fruit; listen to it properly.
Having obtained the fruit of all sacrifices, and likewise the fruit of all gifts, / free from all sins, he goes at the end to Hari's abode.
Having enjoyed enjoyment in Hari's house for thousands of tens of millions of yugas, / having attained the highest knowledge, he attains liberation right there.
He who offers a divine sesame sweetmeat to Kṛṣṇa in the cool season, / to him who has the form of a cowherd, goes to Hari's mansion.
He who gives milk-laḍḍus to great-souled Keśava / drinks nectar in heaven for the duration of a hundred manvantaras.
He who gives pleasant pieces [of candied sugar] to Hari, O Jaimini, / to him Viṣṇu, pleased in spirit, cuts off the bond of worldly existence.
He who gives varied, fruitful, divine [fruit] to the Blessed One, O twice-born, / having gone to Śakra's city at the end, becomes praised by the gods.
A devout person who gives pure sugar to Kṛṣṇa, / what does he not obtain, O brāhmaṇa, through the grace of Vāsudeva?
A fully ripe, sweet jujube fruit in the month of Phālguna— / he who offers it to Kṛṣṇa, listen to his fruit:
In this world he enjoys all happiness, accompanied by sons and grandsons; / at the end, having mounted a splendid chariot, he goes to Hari's house.
One should not give a jujube fruit mixed with raw sugar to Hari; / if one should give it out of ignorance, O best of brāhmaṇas, he becomes a dweller in hell.
In the month of Phālguna, he who gives a pomegranate fruit to Hari, / fully ripe, listen to that fruit as it is told by me, O brāhmaṇa:
As many seeds as remain in that pomegranate fruit, / for that many manvantaras does the fortunate one dwell in Viṣṇu's house.
He who gives a cake made with raw sugar to Hari in the month of Phālguna, / that best of the twice-born should be known as a performer of a thousand horse sacrifices.
In the month of Caitra, O best of the twice-born, if a mortal bathes / Madhusūdana with honey, he attains that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
He who bathes Nārāyaṇa, the faultless one, with honey, / no investigation of him is ever made by the son of the Sun.
He who worships the lord of Kamalā with a kiṃśuka flower in Caitra, / his name is not written by Citragupta in the register.
In Caitra, for one who has worshipped Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the worlds, with tilaka flowers, / there is certainly no birth again on this surface of the earth.
A man worshipping the crest-jewel of all the gods with black vañjula flowers, / O brāhmaṇa, never meets with misfortune.
He who worships the Blessed One with fragrant vāsantī flowers in the spring, / pleased in spirit, is worshipped even by the gods.
Likewise, he who worships Hari with whole, divine sprouts, / rising even from his seated pedestal, he bows to him.
A person who worships Hari with fresh, tender myrobalan leaves / obtains everything desired without delay.
With unbroken leaves of wood-apple, with dhattūra flowers and arka flowers, / he who worships Viṣṇu and the Lord crosses to the other shore of the ocean of saṃsāra.
He who gives an excellent plantain fruit to Viṣṇu, O brāhmaṇa, / all the thirty gods, headed by Śakra, bow to him day and night.
He who in the month of Caitra gives wheat cake with devotion / to the one who takes the form of a cowherd, O brāhmaṇa, is released from all sins.
When the sacred month of Mādhava has arrived, beloved of Mādhava, / a devotee of Viṣṇu should renounce meat, sexual intercourse, and oil.
When the month of Mādhava arrives, a Vaiṣṇava should perform bathing; / he should abandon food belonging to another and should not eat twice [a day].
At dawn, he should worship Viṣṇu according to the rules mentioned before, O twice-born; / in Vaiśākha, he should bathe Viṣṇu with water scented with flowers.
He should bathe Acyuta in cool water until twilight; / with devotion he should worship the Lord at the three twilights with various food offerings.
Adorned in Vaiśākha with garlands of damana blossoms, / what would the Supreme Lord, the consort of Lakṣmī, pleased, not give, O brahmin sage?
He who offers barley food to the Discus-Holder in the month of Vaiśākha— / what wise man is capable of counting his merits?
Whatever is given in the month of Mādhava for the sake of pleasing Mādhava, / [given] to Mādhava alone, all that becomes inexhaustible.
Whatever other good deed is done in the month of Mādhava / for the pleasure of Mādhava, O brahmin, there is no destruction of it.
A person who sets up a water booth in the month of Vaiśākha to satisfy Mādhava / obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice day after day.
Vaiśākha is a rare month, granting the fruit of all rites; / Hari should be worshipped during it, leaving aside even hundreds of rites.
Whatever fruit one obtains by worshipping Hari continually for six years, / one obtains even by performing worship of Hari for a single day in Vaiśākha.
A Vaiṣṇava person who daily [worships] Viṣṇu in the form of an aśvattha tree in the month of Vaiśākha, / for the sake of attaining the fruit of the four aims of life,
who renders service to an aśvattha tree even with a handful of water, / even he, freed from tens of millions of sins, goes to the supreme abode.
He who binds the root of an aśvattha with stones and other materials, O brahmin sage— / what does the Blessed Lord in the form of an aśvattha not give to him?
If, beholding an aśvattha tree, one bows down to it, / he too goes to the supreme abode; his life span increases, there is no doubt.
Whatever pious act a person performs beneath an aśvattha, O brahmin, / there is neither deficiency nor excess in that deed, O Jaimini.
All the sacred fords, beginning with the Tristrotas, are there, O Jaimini, / where even a single aśvattha tree, the best of trees, stands.
He who worships the aśvattha is indeed a worshipper of Viṣṇu, / because the Blessed Lord is Himself the embodiment of the aśvattha, O twice-born.
The foolish-minded one who, out of disrespect, cuts down an aśvattha, O best of the twice-born— / there is no deed in the world by performing which he may be purified.
This aśvattha, king of trees, is celebrated as the embodiment of Hari; / therefore, there is no protector for those who destroy an aśvattha.
For one who looks at the aśvattha, touches it, and furthermore, O brahmin, / for one who bows down, Hari removes every sin abiding in the body.
He who, having seen a destroyer of an aśvattha, does not prevent him although capable, / both of his eyes are plucked out by Yama himself with fishhooks.
He who does not say, 'Fool, do not cut the aśvattha,' / his tongue the King of the Dead cuts out himself with a knife.
He who destroys even a single small branch of an aśvattha, / that person obtains the fruit of ten million murders of a brahmin.
Whatever sin is in the murder of a brahmin, in going with a teacher's wife, / in drinking liquor, and likewise in theft, and also in misappropriating a deposit,
whatever sin is in killing an embryo, in killing a cow, O best of the twice-born, / and whatever sin is in killing a woman, and likewise in going with another's wife,
in killing one who has sought refuge, and likewise in killing a friend, / in speaking false words, and in the act of injuring one's husband,
whatever sin is in reviling others, and in eating on Hari's day— / all that terrible sin is incurred by people from cutting down an aśvattha.
The person who, out of delusion, cuts down an aśvattha, the embodiment of Viṣṇu— / no sinner equal to him has ever been heard of in the orb of the earth.
I shall declare the glorification of the aśvattha, which destroys all sins, / along with a legendary history, O best of the twice-born; listen with concentrated mind, dear child.
Formerly, in the Tretā age, there was a brahmin named Dhanañjaya, O twice-born, / devoted to Hari, delighting in the welfare of all living beings,
always devoted to honouring his kinsmen, ever intent on the gift of lamps, / speaking the truth, having conquered anger, free from violence and deceit.
That seeker of liberation, best of the twice-born, constantly worshipped / the Supreme Lord, the Lord Nārāyaṇa, with supreme devotion.
Then, knowing his great and very firm devotion, the Lord / took away all his wealth by some mere pretext.
Even so, that wise and best of the twice-born performed the worship / of the noble Keśava day after day with supreme devotion.
Having seen that the wealth acquired with suffering was all destroyed, O twice-born, / the brahmin was distressed, his mind troubled by sorrow.
That brahmin, knower of the highest truth, gave up eating, / firmly fixing his own mind upon the worship of Mahāviṣṇu.
Then Janārdana, who is steadfast and grants peace, knowing again the devotion / of that brahmin, brought about separation from his kinsmen.
The kinsmen of that brahmin, bewildered by the illusory power of Viṣṇu, / began to do injury [to him] constantly, O best of the twice-born.
Then the brahmin, freed and detached from kinsmen, continually worshipped / Puruṣottama, pleased and full of abundant devotion.
That earthly god, having dedicated his wealth to the worship of Keśava, / Mādhava, the Lord of the Universe, abandoned grief for his kinsmen.
Then again Mahāviṣṇu, fond of sport, O Jaimini, / although compassionate, took away his sons day after day.
Even so, that best of the twice-born daily worshipped Viṣṇu, / Keśava, the destroyer of suffering, with devotion twice as great as before.
Then his wife, O brahmin, deeply afflicted by pain and sorrow, / went to her father's house, completely bewildered by the illusory power of Viṣṇu.
Then that earthly god, alone, devoted to devotion to Viṣṇu, / never thought of misfortune in his virtuous mind.
Once, that best of the twice-born, foremost of those who possess devotion to Viṣṇu, / placing an axe on his shoulder, went to the forest for wood.
Bringing wood from the forest, that twice-born every day, / lacking clothes at the onset of winter, kept off the cold.
Once, unable to go to the forest, the best of the twice-born / struck a branch of an aśvattha tree standing in his courtyard.
At that moment, Mahāviṣṇu, the foremost of the gods, his mind distressed with pain, / came forth from that aśvattha tree.

The brahmin saw Viṣṇu before him, four-armed, with eyes wide like lotus petals, / wearing yellow garments, adorned with earrings, with beautiful hair, bearing His own weapons beginning with the lotus,

His broad stream of trickling blood like a fresh cloud made crimson in the twilight, / looking like the sun, yet pleasant, the Supreme Lord who cannot be seen by the hosts of gods; / both his eyes charming with streams of tears of joy, the brahmin praised [Him] with gentle words.
The brahmin said: / 'O Hari, Murāri, Sole Lord of the Universe, Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava, / Consort of Lakṣmī, Keśava, Foe of Keśin, Nārāyaṇa, Infinite One, All-pervading Lord, be gracious!'

What can I say of your incarnation? Without you, nothing exists here on earth. / Or what [can I say] of your qualities that pervade the whole universe, or of your compassion that treats friend and foe as one?
Bestowing one's own devotion unto someone, O Lord Viṣṇu, unto Hari whose form is imperishable— / 'Receiving prosperity, I shall bestow delight'—devotion bestowed upon the great is most blessed.
I constantly consider myself, O one of endless forms, as the foremost of sinners; / for that very reason, a sinner does not behold your pair of feet, which are worthy of divine contemplation.
Although I consider myself the most afflicted among the sorrowful, today, O Viṣṇu, / I look upon myself as Indra, since with my own two eyes I directly behold you, the Soul of the universe.
I know not even the slightest worship of you, nor do I ever offer wealth to you; / nevertheless, you have appeared embodied before me—you, Keśava, the sole object of worship, have been seen by me.

This tree of devotion to me was granted by you, yielding only the triad of dharma, wealth, and desire; / sprinkled today by the rain-shower of your sight, O Lord, it has borne the fruit of final liberation.
May my head become the foremost of all heads in the world before Keśava, who possesses the universal form; / indeed, my mind now goes to your pair of lotus feet, O God of gods!
Vyāsa said: / Having praised Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the universe, who is free from affliction, / that virtuous twice-born one with folded hands spoke to him again with devotion:
The brāhmaṇa said: / O God of gods, O Lord of the universe, cause of grace to the world! / By blows of an axe, this body of yours has been bathed in blood.
The races of all the Daityas have been destroyed by you in battle; / who on earth is capable of striking you? O Lord, this is a great wonder!
The Blessed One said: / My child, what you have spoken is true; there is no doubt about this. / No Dānava or Rākṣasa is capable of striking me.
I myself, in the form of the sacred fig tree, was struck by you with an axe; / therefore, O twice-born, a flow of blood has now arisen in my body.
Vyāsa said: / Hearing this word of his, that twice-born, overwhelmed with fear, / condemned himself in many ways through his own mind:
'Cursed indeed is that fortune of mine, the foremost among all sinners, / who has caused great pain in the heart of the Lord of the three worlds!
Viṣṇu, who removes all sins, has been afflicted by me. / It is not possible for me alone to cross over this sin.
When he is pleased, even sinners become revered by the gods; / he has been pained by the pain inflicted by me—alas, I am undone!
Whom the gods headed by Brahmā propitiate with intense devotion— / oh, pain has been given in his heart by a sinful one like me!
What use are austerities, what use are recitations, what use are homes or my life? / This sole giver of dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation has been afflicted with pain!'
Having spoken thus, that best of the twice-born resolved to strike / his own neck with that very axe for the sake of pleasing Viṣṇu.
Recognizing his steadfast devotion, the compassionate Lord of Kamalā, / fond of his devotees, swiftly took away that axe from his hand.
The Blessed Lord said: / Why, my child, do you perform such an exceedingly dreadful deed? / I am never pleased with men who commit suicide.
I am indeed pleased with your devotion; do not fear, O best of men! / Choose a boon, O chief of brāhmaṇas, whatever is in your heart.
The brāhmaṇa said: / This great pain has been inflicted by me, O Supreme Lord; / may it not remain in your body—this is the boon I ask, O Lord!
The Blessed Lord said: / My child, this act was done by you out of ignorance, O twice-born; / therefore, your offense is not to be regarded as great.
I must always protect you, since you are the foremost devotee; / I take upon myself your faults day after day, my child.
Even so, your great devotion to me has ever increased; / therefore, my child, I now desire to be free from debt to you.
Abandoning all fear, choose a boon before me. / The brāhmaṇa said: In you, the foremost of all gods, birth after birth,
let there be very firm devotion, O Hari! What need is there of other boons? / Vyāsa said: Hearing this speech of his, spoken out of love, Keśava,
being pleased, then gave him the garland resting on his own neck. / Then, embracing the brāhmaṇa with his four long arms like a father embracing a son,
the Lord spoke tender words: / The Blessed Lord said: Since you are my devotee, O twice-born, by my grace,
every auspiciousness will come to pass for you without delay, O twice-born! / Constantly worship me in the form of the sacred fig tree through practical yoga, O best of men;
I will fulfill all your desires. / Having spoken thus to that foremost twice-born and embraced him once again, Keśava,
the abode of compassion, suddenly disappeared right there. / Having obtained the garland from Viṣṇu's neck, that twice-born, the best of Vaiṣṇavas,
considered himself fulfilled and remained in his own home. / Then, O brāhmaṇa sage, by the command of Keśava, Kubera himself
showered abundant riches in the house of that brāhmaṇa. / A palace was constructed for him by the architect Viśvakarman,
by order of Nārāyaṇa, superior like Vaijayanta itself, / equipped with male and female servants, adorned with various articles,
filled with crores of elephants and horses; his mansion shone brightly. / His kinsmen, even those long lost, came and reunited with him.
His wife, who had shown him disrespect, returned to his house of her own accord. / Even his wife whose children had died, through the compassion of Keśava,
came to have living offspring, O twice-born, and became devoted in service to her husband. / Having long enjoyed all pleasures accompanied by sons and grandsons,
at the end of his life, that best of brāhmaṇas attained liberation along with his wife. / Vyāsa said: The sacred fig tree itself, the best of trees, is visibly Viṣṇu himself;
for men who practice devotion to it, no misfortune ever exists anywhere. / But whoever, having meditated upon Viṣṇu, attends upon the sacred fig tree, O best of men—
the Lord, being pleased, grants him the supreme abode.

title: trayodaśo'dhyāyaḥ
text_mt: Vyāsa said: / In the month of Jyeṣṭha, O foremost twice-born, one should worship the Blessed Janārdana / with a devotional disposition, bathing him with cool waters.
Anointment should be given, as well as fragrant myrobalan / and sweet-scented oil, day after day to Hari in the summer season.
In a well-perfumed and cool temple that is exceedingly delightful, / one should place the Beloved of Kamalā each day in an assembly pavilion.
One should not place the husband of Kamalā in a place exposed to the sun, O leader of the twice-born, / nor in a woodshed with smoke, nor in a lying-in room.
Fanned with white, very long chowries, / well-pleased in the month of Jyeṣṭha, what will the husband of Kamalā not grant, O best of the twice-born?
Hari, fanned in the heat with fans made of peacock feathers, / grants everything desired in no time at all, O virtuous one.
Those by whom Viṣṇu is fanned in summer with the breeze of a palm fan / or with the breeze of pure cloth—all of them go to heaven.
One who applies fragrant pastes to his limbs, / and to Hari in the summer with sandalwoods, enters the body of Mādhava.
At the onset of heat, O foremost twice-born, he is liberated [from suffering]; there is no doubt of this. / In a garden of blossoming flowers, as well as in a forest of tulasī,
one should place Viṣṇu at twilight in a place with a gentle breeze. / By whoever Viṣṇu is adorned with garlands of trumpet flowers
in the month of Jyeṣṭha, he is to be recognized as one who has performed a thousand horse sacrifices. / But the person who offers a pearl necklace in summer to the Lord of Śrī,
to him Hari grants kingship in birth after birth. / Whoever adorns Śrī Kṛṣṇa with a garland of jewels in the summer,
hear from me, O twice-born, as I declare the fruit of his merit: / As long as Brahmā creates this entire universe, O Jaimini,
so long will he abide in the world of Viṣṇu, adorned with a garland of gems. / And whoever [adorns him] with gold ornaments and with silver ornaments,
adorns Kṛṣṇa in the summer, he too attains that fruit. / But whoever offers a colourful couch with a pillow
to Hari, the God of gods, is never sorrowful. / Heavy garments should not be given in the summer time
to Hari, O best of brāhmaṇas; pure, fine cloth should be given. / Whoever worships Hari with divine, fragrant, imperishable fruits,
having gone to Śakra's city at the end, gladly drinks nectar. / Whoever worships the Lord of Kamalā with divine priyāla fruits,
he too attains that fruit; what need of many words? / Whoever, in the summer heat, [gives] very cool barley gruel to Hari,
combined with various condiments, [if he is] a Vaiṣṇava devoted in faith— / in the month of Āṣāḍha, O best of brāhmaṇas, to the God of gods, the teacher of the world,
having bathed him with curd and worshiped him with devotion, that wise man / never again drinks milk from a mother's breast.
At the onset of clouds, he who worships Hari, who is dark as a raincloud, with kadamba flowers, / O Brahmin sage, attains the supreme path.
Whoever [decorates] the pavilion resembling blazing fire with garlands of kadamba flowers, / O best of Brahmins, obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
Worshiped with fragrant ketakī flowers, the husband of Kamalā / takes away every sorrow of men, O best of the twice-born.
Worshiped with the divine, well-ripened fruits of the jackfruit tree mixed with clarified butter, / the Lord Viṣṇu grants the highest sovereignty.
A Vaiṣṇava wishing for liberation, O best of the twice-born, / should offer curd and cooked rice to Hari every day with faith in the month of Āṣāḍha.
Whichever Vaiṣṇava person gives fresh butter to Kṛṣṇa, / cleansed of all sins, goes to the world of Brahmā.
Whoever worships the Supreme Self with śephālikā flowers / and with yūthikā blossoms goes to the supreme abode.
whoever worships Hari with blooming, fragrant jasmine flowers, / by the merit of that, O twice-born one, he will have such merit as cannot [be measured].
Worshipping Janārdana, the friend of the world, with tuber-blossoms and bakula flowers, / a human being attains every desire in this world.
Whoever worships Hari with grand blossoms / and with blooming kurubakas—with him Hari is always pleased.
Whoever worships Viṣṇu with sairīyaka flowers, / and whoever worships with prasū blossoms and oleander blossoms, goes to Hari's presence.
And whoever offers parched grains mixed with clarified butter to Hari in Śrāvaṇa, / in his house, O Brahmin sage, prosperity faces in every direction.
In the month of Bhādra, O best of the twice-born, a wise man should worship with faith / the spotless Nārāyaṇa, the bestower of the four aims of life.
In a newly constructed house, free from all troubles, / one should place the lotus-eyed Lord Janārdana.
A man should certainly not place Hari in an old room / that is infested with gnats, mosquitoes, and flies.
Nor in a house that is muddy, with a falling doorway, or leaking walls, / should the wise man place Hari, the Supreme Lord, during the rains.
Whatever man makes a variegated canopy in the temple of Viṣṇu, / O best of the twice-born, goes to the world of the Moon.
At night, with various kinds of incense in the temple of the Lord of the earth, / one should ward off stinging flies and mosquitoes at the time of worship.
Having covered Acyuta lying on his couch with mosquito nets, / one should place Viṣṇu in a divine temple at night during the rainy season.
Likewise with fragrant, fresh kahlāra petals, / a mortal seeking liberation should worship the lord of gods day by day in the month of Bhādra.
Janārdana is not to be worshiped with ketakī flowers in Bhādra, / because in the month of Bhādrapada the ketakī becomes like liquor.
Whoever worships the delight of the Yadus with ripe, divine palmyra fruits, / never again experiences the great misery of dwelling in a womb.
Whatever mortal offers ripe palmyra fruit with clarified butter and milk to the enemy of Mura / with faith, goes to the temple of Hari.
In the month of Bhādra, O best of the twice-born, a Vaiṣṇava should offer palmyra cake / with clarified butter to Hari for the sake of attaining solitude [with the divine].
In the month of Bhādrapada, O Brahmin, a Vaiṣṇava person who is a seeker of liberation / must not eat leafy vegetables, nor eat at night.
In the month of Āśvina, O best of brāhmaṇas, [to worship] Keśava, the destroyer of distress: / the water which is offered by men to Hari in the morning,
the Lord of Kamalā receives that water like nectar. / And what water is offered at midday to the Disc-wielder,
it is to be known as mere water; he receives it as such, O best of the twice-born. / But the water which is offered in the afternoon to Govinda,
that water becomes equal to blood; therefore Hari does not accept it. / Therefore, O best of the twice-born, one should worship Hari in the morning;
he obtains every desire through the compassion of Keśava. / Wearing only a single cloth, O best of brāhmaṇas, one should not perform worship of Hari;
or even if he performs worship in that way, Keśava does not accept it. / And whoever performs worship of Hari with an unwashed cloth,
that worship becomes fruitless, and Viṣṇu is not pleased. / But by those people by whom worship of the Disc-wielder is performed with untied hair,
they do not attain the fruit of worship, and that [worship] is taken by Bali. / If worship of the Lord of the world is performed in an unconsecrated room,
that worship, O best of brāhmaṇas, is indeed seized by Bali. / Bathing, deity-worship, giving, and worship of the ancestors—
a wise man does not perform these without a tilaka mark, O brāhmaṇa. / Whatever meritorious rite is performed without having applied tilaka marks,
all that turns to ash, and the agent becomes an inhabitant of hell. / On whose body are seen marks with the conch, disc, mace, and lotus,
he is to be known as Acyuta himself, O best of brāhmaṇas! / The Vaiṣṇava who marks the conch and lotus on his right arm,
and the disc and mace on the left, he is Viṣṇu—there is no doubt about this. / Whoever draws a lotus on the right arm above the conch,
all his evil is destroyed in an instant. / And whoever, O twice-born one, draws the mace above the disc on the left arm,
the immortal gods, headed by Śakra, bow down to him, O best of the twice-born. / And the wise person who draws the pair of Murāri's feet upon his forehead,
even a sinner, upon seeing him, is freed from evil. / Whoever draws the eight-syllabled great mantra, the Fish, and the Tortoise upon his chest,
that best of Vaiṣṇavas purifies the three worlds. / One whose body is marked daily with the weapons of Kṛṣṇa,
to him Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the world, grants the supreme abode. / Whatever action a man performs whose body is marked with Kṛṣṇa's weapons,
whether auspicious or inauspicious, all of it becomes inexhaustible. / Dānavas, Rākṣasas, ghosts, and vetālas,
piśācas, serpents, yakṣas, and vidyādharas, / kinnaras, guhyakas, planetary spirits, and children's demon-seizers,
kūṣmāṇḍas, ḍākinīs, and other obstacle-makers— / all flee in fear upon seeing one marked with Kṛṣṇa's weapons.
Elephants, leopards, and other forest dwellers / flee in fear as soon as they see one marked with Kṛṣṇa's weapons.
Jaundice and other major diseases that strike down the body from bodily form— / whatever person beholds with devotion one whose body is marked with Kṛṣṇa's weapons,
that man attains the fruit equal to the sight of Kṛṣṇa. / Whoever worships Hari in the month of Āśvina with tripartite dūrvā grass,
his lineage continues uninterrupted like dūrvā grass. / Whoever offers a cucumber to Hari in the month of Āśvina,
grief is never born in his heart, O twice-born one. / And when Kārtika arrives, the auspicious best among all months,
a wise person should worship Dāmodara, the God of gods, with devotion. / In the month of Kārtika, O best of brāhmaṇas, for the purpose of pleasing Viṣṇu,
the wise person should perform the morning bath according to the prescribed rule. / Whoever gives up meat and sexual intercourse in the month of Kārtika,
freed from sins acquired in other births, goes to the supreme state. / When the sun enters the sign of Tulā, the morning bath, O best of the twice-born,
sacrificial food, and celibacy destroy great sins. / [Whoever] indulges in meat and sexual intercourse in the month of Kārtika,
birth after birth, O best of brāhmaṇas, he becomes a village pig. / Eating twice, another's food, and oil: a Vaiṣṇava
should strictly avoid these when the month of Kārtika arrives. / But whoever offers a lamp in the sky for Dāmodara,
I shall declare his fruit in brief; listen, O twice-born one: / freed from sins such as brāhmaṇa-slaughter, which bestow suffering,
having gone to Dāmodara's realm, he stays for the duration of a crore of yugas. / Beholding the lamp burning in the sky, the thirty [gods] headed by Vāsava,
all delighted, say thus to one another: / “This one is the best among the meritorious, intent on the worship of Keśava,
who offers a lamp to the Disc-wielder in the month of Kārtika.” / In the month of Kārtika, O best of brāhmaṇas, Hari is always pleased with him.
Whoever gives an inexhaustible lamp in Hari's temple in Kārtika, / day after day that person attains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
Whoever worships Hari with a hundred thousand tulasī leaves in Kārtika / attains the fruit of a hundred thousand horse sacrifices.
Whoever worships imperishable Viṣṇu with a hundred thousand bilva leaves / attains supreme liberation through the grace of the Lord of the world.
Whatever small thing is given in the month of Kārtika dedicated to Viṣṇu, / all of that becomes inexhaustible; this is the truth spoken by me.
Whoever gives a betel leaf smeared with ghee to a Vaiṣṇava in the month of Kārtika, / day after day, O brāhmaṇa, his residence is in Viṣṇu's city.
Whoever worships the Beloved of Kamalā with a blooming lotus leaf, white or blue, / what is hard for him to obtain on earth?
By which foremost twice-born a lotus is not offered to Hari in the month of Kārtika, / what has been given by him, O brāhmaṇa, to Viṣṇu, conqueror of the Daityas?
Having brought even a single lotus, he gives it to the foe of Kaiṭabha; / what does the blessed Lord Viṣṇu, the Husband of Śrī, not give to him?
By whoever Hari is not worshipped with lotuses in the month of Kārtika, / birth after birth, Kamalā does not abide in his house.
Whoever offers lotus seeds to high-souled Keśava / is born into a pure brāhmaṇa family in every birth.
Born in a family of brāhmaṇas, he becomes a friend of the four Vedas, / wealthy, having many sons, and a sustainer of relatives.
There is no flower equal to the lotus; O Jaimini, it is spoken truly: / by worshiping Govinda with it, even an evil soul partakes of liberation.
The glorification of the lotus flower will be related by me in particular; / listen attentively, O best of the twice-born, along with its legendary history.
There was a certain brāhmaṇa named Prajāna, who knew all the śāstras, / the bee of whose mind ever remained in Hari's lotus feet.
Worship of the gods, brāhmaṇas, and gurus was always performed by him, / O best of the twice-born, alongside hundreds of duties and actions.
Another's wealth was [regarded by him] as poison, and other men's wives as his own mother; / thus it was done by him indeed, and likewise toward friend and foe.
Seeing a guest arriving, that brāhmaṇa, who knew the supreme truth, / never felt arrogance toward a beggar or an excellent twice-born.
All sacrifices were performed by him, and all vows, / desiring to cross over the terrible, fathomless ocean of saṃsāra.
Once that best of the twice-born, devoted to devotion to Hari, / contemplated in his mind his own death and his own birth:
"Who was I standing previously? Or what deed was done in the past? / How was this birth obtained? Or where shall I go again?"
Having reflected thus and sighing again and again, that twice-born / went indeed to the sacred site of Śiva in order to learn of his former deeds.
There, folding his hands in reverence and endowed with supreme devotion, / the brāhmaṇa praised the god Śaṅkara, Śiva, with sweet speech.
The brāhmaṇa said: / "Salutations to you, O Mahādeva! Salutations to you, O Parameśvara! / Salutations to you, O Śaṅkara, O Īśāna! Salutations to you, O Lord who grant boons!
Salutations to you whose form is knowledge! Salutations to you who bestow knowledge! / Salutations to you who dwell in the heart-lotus of all living beings!
Salutations to you, creator of the universe! Salutations, salutations to the father of the universe! / Salutations to the agent of dissolution, and salutations to the lord of creatures!
Salutations to you whose eye is fire! Salutations to you who look with fire! / Salutations to you whose eye is the moon! Salutations indeed to you whose eye is the sun!
Salutations to you adorned with ashes! Salutations to you dressed in an animal hide! / Salutations to you wearing a garland of bones! Salutations indeed to you with a blue throat!
Salutations to you with five faces! Salutations to you who hold a trident in hand, / who shatter the pride of Kāmadeva, possessing a formidable form!
Salutations to the God of gods! Salutations to the enemy of Tripura! / To the lord of Pārvatī, salutations to you of formidable form!
Salutations to you whose mind was deeply pleased by the devotion of Bāṇa! / Salutations indeed to you who have many forms! Salutations indeed to you who have all forms!
Salutations indeed to you who bear the Gaṅgā, the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice! / To the lord of spirits, salutations to you who wield the Pināka bow!

Salutations to Īśāna! Salutations, salutations to Wisdom! / Salutations be to you who are visible! Salutations to you who are invisible! / Salutations indeed to you who are conceivable! Salutations to you who are inconceivable!
You alone are Brahmā, the sole lord of the gods; you alone are Viṣṇu; you alone are the sun; / you alone are the moon, the remover of all distress! Salutations, salutations to you, O Parameśvara!"
Hearing his hymn of praise, Śaṅkara, the bringer of auspiciousness to the world, / the gracious Parameśvara, suddenly became manifest.
Beholding him appeared, worshiped by all the gods, / that brāhmaṇa, endowed with immense devotion, bowed to his feet.
Again, with a mind filled with joy, that best of the twice-born, / folding his hands in reverence, praised Mahādeva, the boon-granting Lord.
The brāhmaṇa said: / "The Lord of gods whom even the gods with Indra do not behold, / him I see face to face—this is my great good fortune!
The Parameśvara who is invisible [even] to a mind fixed in meditation, / him I see face to face; what else remains for me to achieve?
Merely by remembering your name, even perpetrators of great sins / go to the supreme abode; I look upon that Lord [himself]!
I have attained my goal, I have attained my goal, I have attained my goal and am fortunate! / Salutations to you, salutations to you! Be pleased, O Parameśvara!"

Mahādeva said: / "I am pleased with this utterance of yours, O best of the twice-born! / Choose a boon, O fortunate one; I indeed wish to give a boon."

The brāhmaṇa said:
"You, the Supreme Self, invisible even to the gods, / I behold directly, O Lord; what need is there of other boons?"
Even so, O Mahādeva, full of compassion, you desire to give a boon; / tell me that which I ask, O Parameśvara:
Who was I living in the past, O God? Or what deed was done formerly? / How have I fallen into the ocean of saṃsāra, O Lord, O Master?
Through karma a body is obtained; the embodied soul is smeared by sin; / again by the influence of sin a terrible destiny is obtained.
By the power of which deeds has this birth been obtained by me, / which bestows various sufferings, O Lord? Being pleased, tell me, O Śaṅkara!
This birth is rooted in sin, and birth is the cause of suffering; / therefore I desire to know my own past history.
Tormented by the stomach's fire, I remained in my mother's womb, / strewn with urine and feces, by the ripening of my actions.
No suffering equal to dwelling in the womb is known in saṃsāra; / how was that experienced by me, O Lord, destroyer of the distress of devotees?
In this exceedingly terrible saṃsāra, full of diverse sufferings, / unsubstantial, deluded by the māyā of Viṣṇu, the resort of sins,
difficult to cross, devoid of kinsmen, connected with desire, anger, and the like, / giving grief and disease, and bestowing birth and death,
fathomless—how have I fallen [into it], O Lord of the worlds, O Śiva? / Tell me all this, O all-pervading Lord, if there is favor toward me."
Mahādeva said: / "Although this is greater than the greatest secret, O best of the twice-born, / and not to be disclosed, yet I shall tell it to you, my devotee.
Formerly you, an excellent brāhmaṇa [now], were born in the lineage of Śabaras; / renowned as Daṇḍapāṇi, you lived causing suffering to people.
Abandoning fear of the other world, devoid of discrimination, / you resorted to the occupation of a robber, which causes supreme affliction to the distressed.
Seeing you taking to the life of a robber and being extremely cruel, / all your other brothers also became robbers.
I shall declare the names of those brothers, O lord among twice-born, / with which brothers banditry was committed by you formerly:
Daṇḍī, Daṇḍāyudha, Dattavān, Dattabhū, / Sundaḍa, and Daṇḍaketu—six brothers are proclaimed.
With those most terrible brothers, completely bereft of compassion, / by your staff all people were perpetually harassed.
Out of greed for wealth, along with those wicked brothers, / in the forest and desolate wilderness, O brāhmaṇa, hundreds and thousands were killed [by you].
Having slain them with sharp arrows while staying in the forest, O twice-born, / the flesh of cows was always eaten by you along with intoxicating spirits.
Then, out of fear of you, all merchants abandoned the practice of traveling; / thus disaster perpetually befell that forest.
When you took to robbery, he who had wealth had no wealth; / he who had a house had no house; he who had a wife had no wife.
In this way, in that very great forest with those brothers of yours, / [one day,] exhausted from the fatigue of traveling, [you] went to a lake to bathe.

Having bathed there, O best of brahmins, being hungry,
lotus stalks and water were consumed by those brothers.

Then, O best of brahmins, O excellent one, out of playful curiosity,
many blossoming lotus flowers were eaten there by you.

At that very time, a brahmin dwelling in the forest,
known as Sarvavedas, arrived there to bathe.

Having bathed there, that righteous soul, endowed with humility,
begged of you a single lotus to worship the blessed Janārdana.

Then, O leader of brahmins, a single spotless lotus was given
by you with supreme devotion for the worship of the lord of Kamalā.

Pleased with the lotus given by you, that best of brahmins
worshiped Viṣṇu, the creator of all, right there.

Seeing that brahmin, Sarvavedas, intent on the worship of Viṣṇu,
you too, smiling, bowed down to Viṣṇu who grants all desires.

Then, having worshiped the supreme Self who grants the fruit of the four aims of life
according to the prescribed rules, that brahmin departed just as he had come.

By that gift of a lotus, by that bow, O excellent one,
and by witnessing the worship of Viṣṇu, all your sin was destroyed.

Then, after some days in that very great forest,
your time having arrived, you underwent death, O best of brahmins.

Satisfied by that very deed, the Blessed One, the abode of compassion,
gave you that supreme abode very difficult to obtain even for the gods.

For thousands of manvantaras and hundreds of manvantaras,
various pleasures were enjoyed there through the grace of the lord of Kamalā.

Then, at the end of that karma, having come to this land of works, O brahmin,
through those fruits of merit you were born in a brahmin lineage.

Having obtained birth in a pure brahmin family, O excellent one,
you obtained unswerving devotion to Hari, the refuge of all virtues.

The Lord, the great Viṣṇu, has been propitiated by you through practical yoga;
He will grant you knowledge; through knowledge you will be liberated.

Go, O brahmin—auspiciousness unto you—well-pleased, to your own house;
you have attained the sight of Me; you are liberated from the bonds of worldly existence.

Then for three days he worshiped Viṣṇu with charming lotus flowers
with great effort, to praise the supreme Lord.

Having worshiped Viṣṇu for a long time with wondrous, beautiful lotus blossoms, and having fallen asleep,
he attained knowledge and went to liberation by the grace of the Lord whose banner bears Garuḍa.

Such is the fruit for one who gives a lotus even unintentionally;
for one who gives [it] with devotion to Viṣṇu, I know not what it may be!

It is true, true, and true again—truly is it spoken by me:
having worshiped Hari with lotuses, the supreme abode is attained.

He who offers even a single lotus to the enemy of Mura,
for him there is no rebirth in terrifying transmigrations.

Those who worship Nārāyaṇa, full of compassion and granter of desires, with blooming lotuses
even for a single day, even sinners endowed with heinous sins, go toward liberation.

title: caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ
text_mt:
Vyāsa said:
In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, O best of brahmins, a Vaiṣṇava should worship
the imperishable Viṣṇu accompanied by Mahālakṣmī with a devotional disposition.

In a barbarian land, O leader of brahmins, likewise in the house of a fallen person,
and in a place permeated by foul smells, one should not worship Viṣṇu.

Near heretics, and likewise near great sinners,
and near those who speak falsehood, one should never worship Viṣṇu.

Nor should one perform the worship of Hari in the presence of those who are lamenting,
those who are quarreling, or in a place where people mock.

One should not worship Viṣṇu in a place of those addicted to receiving gifts,
nor in the house of misers who desire the wealth of others.

Likewise, one should not perform the worship of Viṣṇu [in the place] of deceitful persons.
In the worship of Nārāyaṇa, O brahmin, one should be wholly dedicated to devotion.

Casting aside any distracted mind, one should be intent upon meditating on Hari;
[with] crying of 'Alas!', sighing, and amazement, O best of brahmins,

or conversation with heretics, one should not worship Hari.
Having become single-minded toward the God of gods, the teacher of the world,

whatever flower is offered, even in ashes, reaches Hari;
[yet] one exhausted by hundreds of arriving anxieties, O brahmin, even upon Śālagrāma stones,

whatever flower that mortal gives, the Lord does not receive it.
Having become single-minded, the wise man should worship Viṣṇu with devotion.

Whatever deed is performed with an agitated mind is fruitless;
every deed is subject to the mind, and the three worlds are subject to the mind.

Therefore, having steady the mind, one should worship the lord of Kamalā.
He whose worship is in one place and whose mind is elsewhere, O best of brahmins,

even in hundreds of millions of kalpas his deed will not bear fruit.
Though he has diligently performed purification, and though he is intent on the worship of Viṣṇu,

if he is devoid of purity of mind, he is regarded as merely an outcaste.
Whatever austerity is performed without devotion for a very long time according to the rules, O brahmin,

it all becomes useless, merely a mortification of the body.
Gold the size of Mount Meru, given to a brahmin householder

without devotion, to dispel entreaty or even for one's own welfare, [is useless].
Therefore, having become single-minded, endowed with devotion and faith,

one should offer greens such as vāstuka in an assembly of Vaiṣṇavas.
He who offers a divine, well-ripened orange fruit

to Keśava, O best of brahmins, he is revered by us.
With effort, whatever new item is dear to the blessed Hari,

that very thing one should give with devotion to the enemy of Mura in the month of Āgrahāyaṇa.
When the month of Pauṣa arrives, [to] the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the boon-granting Lord,

the Vaiṣṇava should bathe the God with divine sugarcane juices.
Whoever bathes the Lord Viṣṇu with sugarcane juices, O leader of brahmins,

enjoys all happiness in this world, and, when dead, goes to the ocean of sugarcane juice.
Whoever offers an oblation of sugarcane to Viṣṇu, the God of gods,

he too attains that fruit; what need of many words?
Having given flattened rice with good milk or with curds in Pauṣa

to the enemy of Mura, a mortal obtains all desires.
Having removed the old garment along with everything else, for the enemy of Mura,

in order to ward off cold, one should offer a new garment.
At the winter solstice of Pauṣa, O brahmin, to Viṣṇu who is accompanied by Lakṣmī,

a person desiring liberation should offer a seat of ten colors.
Whoever produces the sound of a conch after worshiping the lord of Kamalā,

I shall tell the meritorious fruit of that; listen attentively, my child:
freed from all sins such as incestuous union with forbidden women,

at the end he goes to the city of Viṣṇu and rejoices with Viṣṇu.
Whoever rings a bell marked with Garuḍa for Hari

at the time of worship, O best of brahmins, I tell his merit:
freed from all sins such as eating forbidden food,

he ascends a splendid chariot and goes to the abode of Viṣṇu.
Having enjoyed all desires there for a period of hundreds of millions of kalpas,

having returned to the earth as a best of brahmins versed in the four Vedas,
he enjoys all desires there for a period of hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Going once more to the city of Viṣṇu, he attains unsurpassed liberation. / But whoever plays the lute at the time of worship of the Lord of the world
that mortal becomes the foremost of scholars in every birth. / Whoever plays the mṛdaṅga drum during the worship of the enemy of Kaiṭabha,
the blessed Lord, well-pleased, gives him his desired fruit. / Likewise, whoever plays the ḍamaru, the ḍiṇḍima, the jharjharī, the madhurī,
the kettle-drum, the dundubhi drum, the kāhala, the sindhuvāraka, / the bell-metal gong, the cymbals, and the flute
at the time of the worship of Mahāviṣṇu—hear of his merit! / Freed from sins [such as those] incurred for theft, he goes to the dwelling of the wielder of the discus;
having attained supreme knowledge, he is liberated right there. / Whoever makes the kala sound at the time of the worship of the teacher of the world
and plays mouth-music, O best of Brahmins, of his merit it is said by me: / together with crores upon crores of family members, he proceeds to the dwelling of Hari;
having attained knowledge right there, he reaches imperishable liberation. / Whoever, filled with devotion, dances in Viṣṇu's temple,
he goes, O best of Brahmins, to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / But whoever sings songs with devotion before Nārāyaṇa,
he attains kingship among the cities of the Gandharvas. / And a Vaiṣṇava person who praises the Lord of the world with hymns in devotion,
